recipes.name: Chicken and Mushroom Tetrazzini
ingredients_raw: 1 (8 ounce) package spaghetti, broken into pieces

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9x13 inch baking dish.
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add spaghetti, and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, or until al dente; drain.
Meanwhile, in a large saucepan, melt butter over low heat. Stir in flour, salt, and pepper. Cook, stirring, until smooth. Remove from heat, and gradually stir in chicken broth and cream.

Return to heat, and bring to a low boil for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Add sherry, then stir in cooked spaghetti, mushrooms, and chicken. Pour mixture into the prepared baking dish, and top with Parmesan cheese.
Bake 30 minutes in the preheated oven, until bubbly and lightly browned.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken and Mushroom Tetrazzini
raw_recipe.description: This baked chicken tetrazzini recipe with spaghetti and mushrooms has a creamy homemade white sauce flavored with Parmesan cheese.

review.reviewBody: This was a big hit in my house. It is a great make ahead dish you can pop in the oven when you get home. I highly recommend substituting lowfat evaporated milk for the heavy cream. It is still plenty rich and satisfying. I got away with only using 3 Tbsp. butter to make my roux and omitted the salt altogether. I cooked the mushrooms with some chopped onion and garlic in a little olive oil before adding into the mixture. I increased the chicken broth to 1-1/2 cups based on other reviews and this amount was perfect. I also increased the sherry to 3 Tbsp. Once the mixture was in the casserole dish I sprinkled some italian herb seasoning and fresh ground pepper over the top. Another variation that is good is to add some grated cheese to the roux after adding in the chicken broth and milk. It works really well with about 1/2 cup of any type of cheese you have on hand (cheese blends work really well). Yummy!

3 stars using this recipe ~ definitely lacked flavor. Please note: This recipe is not for the faint hearted or calorie conscious. There are ways to lighten it up as other reviewers have suggested but it's 5 stars with the following modifications. 1.) Use linguini noodles vs spaghetti cooked al dente as the noodles still have to bake. 2.) Use turkey in this timeless dish, plus it's a good way to use up Thanksgiving leftovers. 3.) Never use canned mushrooms - Ugh! Baby brown bellas and white buttons work beautifully. Saute 3 cloves of minced garlic, 1 small minced onion, and 1 tsp of fresh thyme leaves in butter. Add 1/2 cup of a GOOD white wine and let simmer. Once the liquid from the mushrooms/wine evaporate, set mushroom mixture aside. 4.) When making the sauce, add 1 tsp of salt, 1 tsp of white pepper, and 1 tsp of nutmeg, plus 2 cups milk to the cream and chicken broth for a more sophistacted sauce. Let simmer for 10 + minutes until sauce thickens. 5.) Add the sauce, mushrooms, Parmesan cheese, 3/4 cup frozen peas and 1/4 cup of Italian parsley (flat leaf parsley) to the noodles and stir until the noodles are evenly coated. 6.) Transfer to a baking dish. Mix 1/4 cup of Parmesan cheese and 1/4 cup Italian bread crumbs and spread over the top of the noodles. Dot with butter and bake as directed. FYI - this dish freezes well... With the modifications, this is a flavorful dish more true to the original that will have guests begging for more.... Enjoy!

While cooking the spaghetti, filled an empty colander with frozen peas. Poured cooked, al dente noodles and their salted water over the peas. Salted and peppered two chicken breasts. Seared them, covered, on medium-high for 5 minutes per side. Removed from pot, added ~4oz fresh, sliced mushrooms and sautéed for 3 minutes. Added 1/2 a diced onion and sautéed for another 5 minutes. Chopped chicken. Removed mushrooms and onions from pot, then started in at Step 3. Followed Valerie Brunmeier's suggestions of +1/2 cup chicken broth, 1/2 cup of mixed, shredded Italian cheese, 3tbsp of sherry. Mixed panko, grated parmesan, and smoked paprika for topping. "This tastes like a $25 entree," said my partner.

I need to make this again! I grilled the chicken, added chopped onions and garlic to the butter and sautéed before I added the flour. I used 1/3 heavy cream 1/3 almond milk 1/3 evaporated milk. I will probably eliminate the heavy cream next time. Before I put it in the pan, I added 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper for flavor. When I put everything in the pan, I sprinkled paprika over the top. Sooooo good!!! Served with peas and garlic bread
I added 1/2 cup yellow chopped onion, and 3 cloves minced garlic and sautéed them in the butter, prior to mixing in the flour. Really added a lot of flavor to the dish and everyone LOVED it!
Doubled it. Cooked fresh mushrooms & garlic in butter. Also, I baked my chicken with lots of seasonings on 350 for 20 minutes then diced it. It was delicious.

This is a good "comfort food" recipe. I followed the directions with one exception - which was to use a container of fresh baby bella mushrooms instead of canned. Once the ingredients were combined it felt dry - a criticism some other reviewers had also. I made up an additional half batch of the broth/cream/flour/wine/butter mixture and then added it to the already combined ingredients. That gave the dish a much more pleasing consistency and is something I would continue to do. I divided this into 2 smaller pans and froze one for use at a later date. The finished produce is a little rich so serving it with a healthy green salad on the side cuts some of that. While that doesn't make it a 'healthy' meal, the large salad on the side allows you to have a smaller portion of the main dish to help you keep the fat and calorie count in control.

I made it gluten free by omitting the butter and substituting cornstarch for flour, using half as much of the flour indicated. I heated up the cream with water, reserving 1/2 cup water to mix with the cornstarch. When the cream/water was bubbly, I added the cornstarch and stirred until thickened. And of course, used gluten free spaghetti. The only other change I made was adding 1/4 cup of parmesan to the sauce. Turned out great!

Used leftover turkey and gravy from Thanksgiving.
Sautéed 8 0z. Baby Bella mushrooms and half an onion in butter then made the roux by adding the flour, extra butter and salt. Added the extra gravy to this, along with the sherry.
Added 1 cup chicken broth and 1 cup half an half, the cooked spaghetti broken into smaller pieces, and the leftover turkey. Sprinkled with parmesan cheese.
Cooked in a 9x13 casserole dish for a little less than half an hour. Wonderful dinner!

Love this recipe. Made it 4 or 5 times with the following changes: Break the spaghetti in thirds. Use rotisserie chicken. Saute 1 cup chopped onion, 1 cup sliced fresh mushrooms, and 2 cloves minced garlic in 1-2 T olive oil first, then added all that to the already thickened sauce. For the sauce, I used 1 1/2 cups chicken broth + 1 cup 2% milk + 1/2 cup half-and-half. Also used more sherry - maybe 5 Tablespoons. BE VERY CAREFUL TO USE ONLY 1/2 OF A 16 OUNCE PACKAGE OF SPAGHETTI.

This was really good. The only changes I made was first, I boiled the chicken with three chicken bouillon cubes, once the chicken was cooked, I removed the chicken, but DID NOT throw away the water/broth. I then boiled the spaghetti in the same water I cooked the chicken in. This gives the spaghetti some added flavor.

Also, i added crushed potato chips on one half of it, because my husband and kids like the crunch chips on top. 

Really good recipe!

I made this recipe last night for a service of eight people. I made no changes to the recipe. However, I did add fresh Chantelle mushrooms that grow here where I live here. Everyone loved it. I was surprised that there was adequate sauce for three packages of spaghetti, including the rest of the ingredients. Definitely a keeper I will be making this again.

Awesome! One of the few tetrazzini recipes that does not include cream of something soups. The only changes I made, after reading reviews, was to add onion that I sauted with the flour and I added some parmesan cheese. I'll definitely be making this again!

You have to season as you go along, (salting the water for the spaghetti, adding S&P to the onions/garlic/mushrooms, etc). I had no problem with the flavor, and I did add an extra 1/2 cup broth as suggested to keep it moist, and it bubbled nicely out of the oven. I just am not a fan of meals with more pasta than meat. I sprinkled some mozzarella on top along with the parmesan, bc it melts well making it more 'interesting.' I think this would be good for groups/company, bc it stretches the meal and would feed a crowd, along with a veggie/salad on the side. It's just not my kind of recipe for a family dinner rotation, but it was moist and flavorful.

I can't remember if I've written before, but this recipe is so delicious, I don't bother using any other. I have made this Chicken Tetrazzini IV about 5 or 6 times; made it again today and we can't get enough of it! The only thing I changed was, instead of canned mushrooms, I cook fresh mushrooms and that makes a huge difference in flavor.

This was the best!! I made as directed but added onions and minced garlic to the butter. Subbed half/half for the cream because I had it. Left out sherry because I did not have it. I love whole wheat spaghetti so used that. I think this was the best chicken tetrazzini I've ever had! I loved that I had all the ingredients on hand.

Good base recipe. Using other reviewers suggestions, I sugared the mushrooms in 2 tbs butter, with some minced garlic and onion. I also seasoned the chicken well. I added a little bit of peas to the final mixture and topped with some panko and Parmesan. Will make again.
I made it to direction except I added panko to the Parmesan. My husband loved it. I will add more seasonings next time. I like the suggestions of onion and garlic.
Love this recipe. I add peas to mine!
